prize_parts.citation: For the discovery that liquid-liquid phase separation organizes the interior of living cells into membraneless compartments, and for the physical-chemical framework that explains it

statement.case_for: Phase separation is a clear physical principle (demixing governed by multivalency, interfacial tension and concentration thresholds) that reframed how cells organize biochemistry without membranes. It began with a specific, datable observation (the 2009 P-granule droplets of Brangwynne and Hyman) and was made quantitative by Rosen's multivalent-interaction phase diagrams on reconstituted systems. It is generative: it now informs cell biology, neurodegeneration, drug discovery and synthetic biology, and it can be explained to a broad audience in two sentences. More than 15 years of independent work supports the core principle.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is that many reported in vivo condensates may not be equilibrium phase separation at all, and the field has a reputation for overinterpretation. There is also a legitimate question whether this is chemistry or cell biology and biophysics, and a three-person cut leaves out Pappu and Mittag, whose work on sequence grammar of disordered regions is the most chemical part of the story.

responses.point: Targeted protein degradation (B036) turns the ubiquitin-proteasome system into a designable chemical modality and gives control over molecular recognition; Crews, Deshaies and Handa are the right core.
responses.response: I agree that B036 has a clear mechanism and a new capability, and it is my second choice. I disagree on timing: after more than two decades there is still no approved PROTAC, and the Handa cereblon work and the Crews/Deshaies PROTAC concept are two different achievements joined under one citation. I would want the committee to be sure the prize describes the discovery, not a clinical pipeline that has yet to deliver.

responses.point: B036 converts ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis into a designable chemical reaction, is a general tool, and is mature enough despite the lack of an approved drug.
responses.response: The chemical-biology argument is persuasive, and the independent structural confirmation of ternary complexes counts for a lot. But the ranking from five of us in the top three shows how popular the topic is, not that the attribution is settled. Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim all have credible claims, and a three-person cut is hard to defend. By contrast, B014's founding observation and its quantitative framework are cleanly separable, so I find its attribution easier to explain.

responses.point: Energy landscape and funnel theory (B023) turned protein folding into a quantitative framework tested by experiment, and the recognition is arguably overdue.
responses.response: I take this seriously as a physicist: funnel theory is a deep and well-tested principle, and I list B023 as an alternative. My hesitation is that the 2024 prize on protein structure prediction and design has already covered the neighboring ground, and the original discovery is a theoretical framework that is hard to separate from decades of refinement. Phase separation seems to me a more open field with a newer and more distinct claim, though I would like to hear whether you think Wolynes, Onuchic and Fersht form a coherent citation.

responses.point: Phase separation recasts intracellular organization as a general physical-chemical principle, with Hyman and Brangwynne as founders and Rosen providing the molecular grammar.
responses.response: I agree with the main line, and your point about multivalency and interfacial tension is the one I would put in the citation. Where I would press you is on Pappu and Mittag: if the physical chemistry is what makes this a chemistry prize, should the credit lean toward the molecular framework and less toward the founding observation? I currently keep Rosen as the molecular anchor, but I am open to being persuaded.

responses.point: Surfactant-templated mesoporous silica (B017) is highly original, mature, and supported by rigorous structural evidence, so recognition is not premature.
responses.response: I accept that B017 is mature and original, and structural clarity is a virtue. I question how much broad generative potential remains compared with the 2025 recognition of framework materials, which covers adjacent porous-solid territory, and the attribution among Kresge, Beck, Ryoo, Stucky, Zhao and Inagaki is contested. I would like you to say what exactly the Mobil discovery contains that FSM-16 and later work do not.

uncertainties: Whether the committee regards phase separation as chemistry rather than cell biology or biophysics.
Whether the in vivo condensate debate is settled enough that the citation should limit itself to the principle and reconstituted systems.
Whether Pappu and Mittag should displace one of the three, given that the three-person limit forces a choice.
Whether B036 should wait for an approved PROTAC drug or whether the mechanistic work already suffices.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for any shortlisted candidate. I note only that Emma Sparr and Peter Somfai are Lund colleagues and that Lund hosts nanoscience and soft-matter work, but I have no collaboration with the candidates, so no recusal appears necessary.
